title: Group Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All of CSL's Personnel (term not defined in the lodged document). Subject to the insider trading law, Closed Periods, the short selling, short-term dealing, margin lending and secured financing bans, and the hedging restrictions on unvested or holding-locked Equity Plan entitlements. May hedge vested, unlocked CSL Securities within Open Periods without approval unless a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Undefined in the lodged document. Restricted Persons and their Related Parties may deal in CSL Securities only during Open Periods and only with prior approval under section 3.1.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors including the CEO. Distinguished for approval routing: the Chair approves directors' dealings; the CSL Board or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee approves the Chair's dealings. Non-Executive Directors consult the Board Chair on whether they may deal. Also within the absolute hedging ban.

tiers.name: Directors and members of the Global Leadership Group
tiers.description: Directors, members of the Global Leadership Group (undefined in the lodged document) and their Related Parties. Subject to an absolute prohibition on hedging arrangements in relation to CSL Securities, regardless of vesting state.

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: Undefined in the lodged document. Closed Periods, the prior approval regime for Restricted Persons, the hedging bans and the Exceptional Circumstances process each extend expressly to Related Parties.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding CSL Securities.

windows.start_anchor: end of the relevant financial year

windows.end_anchor: start of the trading day following the release of the AGM materials

windows.start_anchor: any time other than a Closed Period
windows.end_anchor: commencement of the next Closed Period

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Disclosure Committee may specify any other Closed Period from time to time, including declaring or extending a Closed Period to cover a hedge exercise date. The policy does not say whether such periods are confidential. Personnel working on a transaction or project may also be notified that they may not trade in the securities of other entities involved.

rules.tier: Directors and members of the Global Leadership Group
rules.detail: There is no definition of dealing or of CSL Securities in the lodged document and derivatives are not named. Any derivative that limits the economic risk of holding CSL Securities (a purchased put, a collar, a swap) is a hedging arrangement and absolutely prohibited for directors, Global Leadership Group members and their Related Parties. Non-hedging derivatives are not addressed.
rules.evidence: Hedging is a form of dealing and includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding CSL Securities.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named and there is no dealing or securities definition in the lodged document. Risk-limiting derivatives over CSL Securities are governed by the hedging rules in 2.5; other derivatives are not addressed beyond the general insider trading, Closed Period and (for Restricted Persons) approval requirements that apply to any dealing in CSL Securities.

rules.tier: Directors and members of the Global Leadership Group
rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements in relation to CSL Securities for directors, Global Leadership Group members and their Related Parties, with no distinction between plan and non-plan shares or between vested and unvested holdings, and no approval route.
rules.evidence: Directors, members of the Global Leadership Group and their Related Parties must not enter into hedging arrangements in relation to CSL Securities.

rules.detail: No Personnel may hedge CSL Equity Plan entitlements before vesting, and must seek to ensure Related Parties do not.
rules.evidence: Personnel who have entitlements to CSL Securities under a CSL Equity Plan must not (and must seek to ensure their Related Parties do not) hedge against those entitlements prior to the vesting of those entitlements or while they are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Vested Equity Plan securities that remain subject to a holding lock may not be hedged by any Personnel.
rules.evidence: must not ... hedge against those entitlements prior to the vesting of those entitlements or while they are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Personnel other than directors, Global Leadership Group members and their Related Parties may hedge vested, unlocked CSL Securities if the hedge is initiated in an Open Period, is arranged so that its specified exercise date falls within an Open Period, and they hold no inside information. If the Disclosure Committee later declares or extends a Closed Period over the exercise date, prior approval to exercise may be requested under 3.1.
rules.evidence: Personnel (other than a director, member of the Global Leadership Group or their Related Parties) may hedge against vested CSL Securities that are not subject to a holding lock if the hedge is both initiated in, and arranged so that the specified exercise date falls within, an Open Period and when not in possession of inside information.

rules.detail: A Restricted Person who is not a director or Global Leadership Group member may hedge vested, unlocked securities on the 2.5 conditions but, as hedging is a form of dealing, must first obtain approval under 3.1 and deal within three ASX trading days.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Related Parties may only deal in CSL Securities during Open Periods if prior approval is sought and granted in accordance with the procedure set out in section 3.1 Seeking Prior Approval and they are not in possession of inside information.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, funded collar or similar limits the economic risk of holding CSL Securities and so is a hedging arrangement (banned for directors and GLG; window-conditioned for others), and any structure secured on CSL Securities is a secured financing arrangement banned for all Personnel under 2.6.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not obtain margin loans using CSL Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of CSL Securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling CSL Securities for all Personnel, defined as selling financial products not owned with a view to repurchasing later at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Personnel are not permitted to engage in any short selling of CSL Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and there is no dealing definition in the lodged document.

CFDs are not named. A CFD used to limit the economic risk of holding CSL Securities would be a hedging arrangement under 2.5, and a short CFD closed within three months could offend the short-term dealing ban, but the policy does not address CFDs directly.
Margin loans using CSL Securities as security, solely or within a portfolio, are banned for all Personnel with no approval route.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not obtain margin loans using CSL Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans

rules.detail: Granting security over CSL Securities to support any financing is a secured financing arrangement and banned. A charge or lien unconnected with financing is not addressed.
rules.evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of CSL Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any secured financing in respect of CSL Securities for all Personnel, not limited to margin loans, with no tier, vesting-state or approval carve-out. The Exceptional Circumstances process cannot override it because dealings permitted under 2.7 must comply with the other sections of the Policy.
rules.evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of CSL Securities.

rules.detail: Buying and selling CSL Securities within a three-month period is banned unless Exceptional Circumstances apply (severe financial hardship, court order or other exceptional circumstance) and prior approval is granted under 3.1.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not buy and sell CSL Securities on a short-term basis (that is, within a three-month period) except in Exceptional Circumstances (see section 2.7 Exceptional circumstances) and provided prior approval is sought and granted

clearance.approver: Chair (for directors including the CEO and their Related Parties); CSL Board or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee (for the Chair and the Chair's Related Parties)
clearance.evidence: A request to trade is made through the online employee share registry portal or directly in writing to the relevant approver. Any request for approval to trade may be granted or refused without explanation.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary or their delegate (CEO and Chair for the Company Secretary and their Related Parties)
clearance.evidence: If approval to deal in CSL Securities is granted, the dealing must be conducted within three ASX trading days of the approval. If the Personnel does not deal in CSL Securities within this time period, the approval is no longer effective and approval must be sought again.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary or their delegate (only for Exceptional Circumstances dealings, hedge exercises caught by a declared Closed Period, and dealings in Other Securities)
clearance.evidence: Prior approval to deal in CSL Securities either: (a) during an Open Period (for Restricted Persons and their Related Parties); (b) on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances; or (c) during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances, must be sought

carve_outs: Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or other exceptional circumstances) with prior approval under 3.1
short_term.evidence: Personnel must not buy and sell CSL Securities on a short-term basis (that is, within a three-month period)

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: applying for or acquiring CSL Securities under a CSL Equity Plan (including by exercise of options or rights)

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or participation in a scheme of arrangement

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: transfers of CSL Securities resulting in no change in beneficial interests in those securities (eg the transfer from one personal security holding to another)

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of Personnel dealing in units or shares of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed on a discretionary basis by a third party

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: participation in, acceptance of, or trading under, an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, CSL's Distribution Reinvestment Plan and an equal access buy back

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Personnel or their Related Party did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Closed Period, the plan does not permit the Personnel or their Related Party to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a Closed Period, other than in exceptional circumstances

exceptions.approver: Section 3.1 prior approval still applies to excluded dealings
exceptions.evidence: a transfer of CSL Securities arising from the administration of a deceased estate

exceptions.approver: Relevant approver under 3.1 (Chair for directors; Board or ARMC Chair for the Chair; CEO and Chair for the Company Secretary; Company Secretary or delegate for others), on sufficient evidence
exceptions.evidence: Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may be granted prior approval to sell or otherwise deal in CSL Securities during a Closed Period or on a short-term basis where the Person is in severe financial hardship
or required to sell/transfer under a court order
or where there are other exceptional circumstances

external_documents: CSL Equity Plan rules (holding lock terms)
Definitions of Personnel, Restricted Persons, Related Parties, Global Leadership Group, CSL Securities and Inside Information are not included in the lodged document
exemption_authority: The section 3.1 approvers (Chair for directors including the CEO; CSL Board or ARMC Chair for the Chair; CEO and Chair for the Company Secretary; Company Secretary or delegate for all others) may approve Closed Period or short-term dealings in Exceptional Circumstances on sufficient evidence, consulting management where appropriate. Such dealings must still comply with the other sections of the Policy unless otherwise notified, so there is no stated authority to waive the hedging, short selling or secured financing bans. The Disclosure Committee sets additional Closed Periods.
jurisdiction_overlays: Personnel must also comply with any applicable obligations or requirements under local law in their jurisdiction (CSL securities also trade on US OTC as ADRs)

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to all of CSL's Personnel ... additional restrictions on dealing in CSL Securities which apply to Restricted Persons and their Related Parties
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lodged document contains no definitions section, so whether a given executive is a Restricted Person or Global Leadership Group member, whether Related Parties include trusts and controlled companies, and whether CSL Securities includes OTC derivatives must be confirmed from CSL's internal definitions before structuring.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel must not obtain margin loans using CSL Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of CSL Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is prohibited for every tier with no approval route, so only an unfunded collar could ever be considered.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedge exercise date in Open Period
bespoke_clauses.clause: may hedge against vested CSL Securities that are not subject to a holding lock if the hedge is both initiated in, and arranged so that the specified exercise date falls within, an Open Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For eligible non-GLG Personnel, the collar's expiry or exercise date must be pre-set to fall within an Open Period, and an ad hoc Closed Period over that date requires approval to exercise.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging is a form of dealing ... Therefore, where hedging is not prohibited under this Policy it must be undertaken in accordance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A permitted hedge still attracts Closed Periods, the three-month short-term rule and, for Restricted Persons, prior approval and the three-trading-day validity window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless otherwise notified to the Personnel, any dealing permitted under this section 2.7 Exceptional circumstances must comply with the other sections of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hardship relief opens Closed Periods and the short-term rule only; it does not unlock hedging for directors and GLG or secured financing for anyone.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a request for approval to trade is granted, it may be withdrawn at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in the circumstances of CSL Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared transaction can be pulled before execution, so the bank should not commit pricing until the order is authorised.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval may not be granted where the dealing may not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically permitted hedge by a Restricted Person can be refused on reputational grounds without explanation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy (except for section 3.1 Seeking prior approval) does not apply to: ... (c) transfers of CSL Securities resulting in no change in beneficial interests
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a transfer of shares to a custodian or nominee with no change in beneficial interest still requires the prior approval process for Restricted Persons.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Directors, members of the Global Leadership Group and their Related Parties are absolutely prohibited from entering hedging arrangements in relation to CSL Securities, which captures the put and call legs of a collar regardless of vesting state, and no approver can waive it. Separately, section 2.6 bans all Personnel from margin loans and any other secured financing arrangement in respect of CSL Securities, so the loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited for everyone. Personnel below the Global Leadership Group may enter an unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares only if it is initiated in an Open Period with its exercise date fixed within an Open Period, they hold no inside information and, if they are Restricted Persons, they obtain prior approval (Company Secretary or delegate) and deal within three ASX trading days. Key terms including Restricted Persons and Related Parties are undefined in the lodged document and must be confirmed with CSL.
